source.title: Envelope-Guided Regularization for Improved Prediction in High-Dimensional Multivariate Regression

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It analyzes and simulates a double-descent prediction-risk curve using a different setting and estimator from the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own limiting-risk analysis and simulations of NIECE over the ratio u*/n. Double-descent results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. Tuning choices and method comparisons unrelated to the double-descent curve are also omitted.
record.test_reason: The authors derive (Theorem 2) and simulate (Sec. 5.4) the prediction risk of a least-squares-type envelope estimator (NIECE) as u*/n varies. Risk diverges at u*/n = 1 and falls beyond it. This is the study's own double-descent result in a new setting (predictor-envelope multivariate regression), bearing on V4. The optimally tuned shrinkage variant (EgReg) and the noise-driven divergence term also bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that NIECE's limiting and simulated prediction risk shows double descent over u*/n. EgReg (envelope-guided shrinkage) has lower risk than NIECE for every γ in the limit and across the simulated range, especially near u*≈n. EgReg also outperforms NIECE in finite samples (Theorem 1) and is competitive with or better than PCR, ridge and PLS in simulations and on NIR data.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives and simulates prediction risk for multivariate-regression estimators as envelope dimension relative to sample size varies; it does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments.
record.problems: The double-descent simulation reports 100 replications but no uncertainty measure for those results; its plotted numerical values are not given in the text. The theoretical result depends on stated asymptotic assumptions and concerns NIECE in multivariate regression.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported double-descent results were left out.

untested.parts: The simulation varies u* at fixed n. No sample-size sweep showing more data hurting is reported.
Only one estimator family (linear envelope regression) is studied, not multiple model classes.
No effective-complexity measure is tested across axes.
Label noise as such, multiple or triple peaks, and empirical variation of the noise level are not studied.

missing.what: Limiting risk of EgReg at optimal λ* (ridge on the envelope components, given known Σx and Φ). Finite at γ=1 and lower than NIECE for all γ, i.e., no divergent peak under optimal regularization.
missing.locator: Theorem 2, eq. (16); Figure 1 and accompanying text

missing.what: Simulated EgReg and EgReg(r) risk curves, smaller than NIECE across the u*/n range with the advantage largest near u*≈n

record.verdict_notes: The proof reduces to Hastie et al. (2022) ridgeless least squares when r=1, so this is essentially the linear-regression double descent in an envelope setting. The x-axis is the true envelope dimension relative to n, with the fitted dimension equal to it; it is not a capacity sweep on a fixed problem. The V6 verdict relies partly on eq. 16 and the authors' statements, since the figure values are not readable in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network test error over model size.
Changing training sample size near an interpolation threshold.
The study examines NIECE in multivariate regression, not a range of other model classes; its result does not establish the curve across model classes generally.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, and sample size.
The study does not test label-noise or variance dependence, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not compare the curve with an effective-parameter count or test whether such a count makes it U-shaped.

rows.subject: NIECE estimator
rows.operation_detail: Derived limiting prediction risk as u*/n tends to γ.

conditions.value: Theorem 2 assumptions, including Φ(u*) = D(u*) = Iu* and tr{Γ′β*β*′Γ} = c²

rows.value: tr{Σε} γ/(1−γ); the paper states the risk rapidly diverges to ∞ as γ approaches 1 from below.
rows.note: Asymptotic result for the regression estimator, not a deep network.
rows.check: Pre-threshold branch. Bias is zero and risk equals tr{Σε}γ/(1−γ), so the peak is purely a noise-variance term. It rises monotonically from 0 with no first descent and no U-shape. It also bears on V6's noise or variance part.

rows.subject: NIECE estimator
rows.operation_detail: Derived limiting prediction risk as u*/n tends to γ.

conditions.value: Theorem 2 assumptions, including Φ(u*) = D(u*) = Iu* and tr{Γ′β*β*′Γ} = c²

rows.value: c²(1−1/γ) + tr{Σε}/(γ−1); the paper states risk rapidly decreases after γ exceeds the threshold.
rows.note: This is the post-threshold branch of the reported limiting curve.
rows.check: Post-threshold branch, c²(1−1/γ)+tr{Σε}/(γ−1). Risk decreases monotonically toward c², the risk of the null predictor, and never falls below the under-parameterized regime. The divergence comes from the tr{Σε} term, so this row also bears on V6.

source_check.correct: The recorded formula is correct. Derived from equation (15), its derivative is c²/γ² − tr{Σε}/(γ−1)²; global monotone decrease is not guaranteed when c² > tr{Σε}.
source_check.problem: The verdict-fix annotation overgeneralizes local post-threshold descent into monotone decrease throughout γ > 1.

source_check.reason: The scope limitation is justified by the monotonically increasing pre-threshold branch in r1: there is no initial descent. However, the supplied rationale overstates r2: convergence to c² does not guarantee global monotone decay or universal inferiority to every underparameterized risk.

relationships.condition: Limiting risk, Theorem 2; noise-variance part and optimal-regularization part

relationships.display_finding: Divergent terms scaled with tr{Σε}, while optimal EgReg risk tr{Σε}γm(−λ*) remained finite at γ=1 and below NIECE for every γ.

relation.reason: Theorem 2 and Section 5.4 directly test limiting and empirical risk behavior; equation (16) also bears on noise and optimal regularization.

tranche.reason: The paper derives and simulates its own interpolation-peak and post-threshold recovery result in predictor-envelope multivariate regression, a new setting.

source_check.notes: Prediction risk in equation (9) measures error relative to the regression signal and excludes fresh response noise; the null-predictor risk is c² under the stated assumptions. Theorem 1 establishes lower reducible risk and a smaller total-risk upper bound, rather than unconditional finite-sample total-risk dominance.

statements.correction: NIECE-specific facts: pre-threshold risk tr{Σε}γ/(1−γ) increases from zero; post-threshold risk tends to c² as γ grows. The c² limit is an asymptote, not a universal lower bound.
